reviews.review:
After noticing the demo for this game and really enjoying it, I ended up buying the full game on the same day, replaying everything I'd just done, and then going through the entire rest of the game to my knowledge, including every ending I could find before putting the game down. Suffice to say, I loved it!

To start, this game has a fair few violent scenes, a few of them particularly upset me which is a plus for a horror/suspense game like this, the facial expressions in these scenes were the big thing that sold how horrific things were for me, they were very well done. Talking about non-violent scenes, the character's main sprites don't move around that drastically and you'll probably get used to the main facial expressions quickly since there aren't THAT many, but there's more than enough to convey all the emotions this game needs to and I think they work great.

I should note a good chunk of this game's assets are royalty free, which I found generally charming and not at all a detractor from the main experience even if at first I wished the characters were a bit more unique (there's like two headshapes/eye styles basically, although the characters are colorful enough it doesn't matter too much) and there's a few instances where the style shift in background styles between those from different sources (I believe some backgrounds were individually commissioned) I found a tiny bit jarring. Again, though, I was a big fan of this game and the way all of these assets was put together worked wonderfully for me, although maybe if you're familiar with where any of these assets came from or have seen them in other things maybe it'd bother you more? I don't know, again, the way they were used was wonderful, I just wanted to comment on the stylistic divide between certain game assets and the reason why that's the case.

While talking about the technical side, there are two more things I want to note about this game... one, as seen in the 4th screenshot on the Steam Page, the menu has a list of all of the characters and their names for reference... I feel like the text color picked for Shido making his name not legible was a bit annoying, even if it was nice that the color choice fit in with all of the others in this menu being rather colorful. And two, there are a few typos or errors in the text I noticed. I think there was one instance where the characters were splitting up and the wrong name was said, and several others of either the slightly wrong word or the wrong spelling of a word being used. Nothing major that inhibits clarity or anything, but to my memory most of the typos I caught were all grouped fairly close together so they might be more noticeable because of that.

The actual story... well, it impressed and amazed me. I'm not a visual novel expert so I don't know if anything else in this medium has tackled a similar story, I'm sure something has, but regardless of that I loved THIS story. I won't mention the specific of the plot beats but in regard to what I figure the story was about: once I realized what kind of story this game was trying to tell I became committed to its narrative even though I was already on-board. The protagonist's journey was so compelling to me, the protagonist's breaking faith and panic, resolve and reckless actions, awful actions and dehumanization of others, and then constantly remembering his own humanity again... it all really stuck with me. When he was rude to various characters (particularly the girls, as it takes him time to sympathize with two of them which stuck out a lot to me as a character flaw) I felt bad but kept wanting to believe in him and understanding why he got to where he was, which was a journey he also had to take. I'll be thinking about Ren's behavior for quite some time, the impact of this story of him and his companions was something else.

To say some negatives about the story... in some ways, it got close to the end rather fast after going on for longer than I expected before that point, and assuming I got them all, the multiple endings advertised in the description are all fairly brief, but still unique in their outcome so even that I don't totally mind. The protagonist Ren is the core of this story and one of its main highlights, but I also loved the other characters, who all had their own depth and were all in similar situations, tested by the game and all used in unique ways that I think emphasized the games main themes very well... and as such, in some ways I do wish the endings gave them all a bit more focus as a result. They're just as important there as anywhere else in the game with new developments for them even there, but there isn't really time for much to happen with them nor even the characters themselves to get to expand upon those revelations.

However, I do think giving the other characters more focus and having longer endings, as much as part of me wants those things, would also end up undermining what this game was actually about, you're constantly finding out new things about every character and Ren too comes to consider their perspectives differently as the game goes on... in the end, though, no matter how much time you've spent with them and how much you think you have them figured out, they might surprise you. Or, they might not... but regardless, in any different scenario they might end up showing any different side of themself, and it's hard to know who is right and who is wrong, what pushes people to do things and who is at fault and how much any given person can be held culpable and what is safe to assume about someone in any given moment... fiction can't answer those questions, but these characters try to do so on their own terms even when those aren't the terms they're living with, and they alongside this game's wonderful, talented developer leave you to do the same.

tl;dr I loved this game, its protagonist, themes, dilemmas, and characters a lot, and I'm excited for anything else that Lone Fox Studio might make!
